author: Myst1z
text:
extremerrage wrote: good day every one , been latley not active as usual , but i am back on the track now

Hi EM! Great trades! If you don't mind could I ask some questions
regarding the UJ trade? They're in the chart below and is something that
 has bothered me for some time. I see engulfs everywhere, how do you
guys know which ones to take and which to avoid? Say we're in a
downtrend, it makes sense to always short the lowest supply which
engulfed some demand, but sometimes I see people bypass it and short a
higher supply, how do you determine which is the logical supply to
short?

author: extremerrage
text: good day MY concerning the engulfs , i rely on HTF engulfs before entering a trade on LTF have a look @ this 4h chart the story is there .

author: extremerrage
text:
let me add , on the 1H, there is a big compression, and whenever there
 is a big compress you should pinpoint the DP where the decison was made
 and that was exactly in the area of ignored supply .

author: Myst1z
text:
Hi EM! Thanks for your reply, it does makes sense. However I'm still
puzzled about one thing - You mentioned that you rely on HTF engulfs,
however on the chart below isn't the orange rectangled supply also one
that caused an engulf down? Why wouldn't this be a feasible short for
you? Thanks in advance!

author: extremerrage
text:
hello MY , the zone you marked on the chart , was a reaction from the
 left which is not fresh , so why should i short there and i know the
above level is fresh ?

author: Myst1z
text:
Hi EM! That was a fantastic reply, I never did consider a supply zone
as not fresh because it was a reaction to ignored demand, I only
consider it not fresh if it is a reaction to another supply zone. But
what you said makes a lot of sense and will probably reform the way I
look at charts and define fresh and unfresh zones. So glad I asked you,
thanks and have a great weekend!
